# One more week of news through the new system, read for its answer choices: design, third version (D549, D550; under D439), 2026-11-15

A diagnostic of the frozen step that writes answer choices, on news outside the days it was tuned on. It passes no gate:
Alex's lines (D400) are set on 44 topics and three attempts each, and he did not set this sampling. The numbers below are a
scaled, proposed rule of the council's, written before any send. The first version pooled the new week with the fresh week;
the council refused it (`reflection-2/cold-codex-9.md`): the fresh week already holds two agreed faults of a zero-fault line,
so a pooled rule could never be met. The second version judged the new week apart; the council's next round
(`cold-codex-10.md`) corrected its outcome claims, its reading capacity and its budget wording. This is the third.

## 1. What is sent

- **News:** 2026-10-06 to 10-12, 272 articles, in order (`manifest-2026-10-06-10-12.json`; the same set and order through both
  systems' own entries; text identity `659eaeda6f6c9fe1`).
- **The run:** the new system as frozen, through the runner that ran the fresh week, unchanged
  (`clean-arch/e2e-comparison-2026-11-13/run_fresh.py clean --manifest ... --passes 3`, its own root and ledger): Step 1 at c8,
  Steps 2 and 3, the topics as cases, the answer-choice step three attempts a topic, the frozen judge. The judge is kept: the
  unchanged runner is the proved path, and its share of the fresh week's charge was $0.07 of $2.52. No abbreviated harness.
- **A known limit of the unchanged runner:** the first step stops at 300 calls (a frozen limits file). The week needs 272 plus
  retries; the four stored runs used 0 or 1 retries in 235 to 243 articles. A stop there is the run's stop.

## 2. What "unseen" means here, and its bounds

No later week is wholly unseen, so the claim is bounded: **topics opened on articles not found in the exposure search, within
a week that contains previously exposed articles.** The earlier articles can still shape the library and which later topics
open. The search (`exposure_census.py`, `exposure_bounds.py`; 14,408 files, 7.0 GB, by exact article id):

| Class | Articles | How it is handled |
|---|---|---|
| Found in a stored model request, trace or library, a readers' packet, a reference file or a council transcript | 22 (`exposed-2026-10-06-10-12.json`; 7 in a first-step trace) | a topic opened by one of them is reported and left out of both counts |
| Not in any of those, but shown on a review page of the offline source-page work (the page cleaner replayed by code; an id search of that work's one model trace, the 17-article full-page diagnostic, finds none of the week's ids) | 19 (`exposure-bounds.json`) | a topic opened by one of them is in the wider count and out of the strict count |
| A recurring headline whose earlier edition an old run read in August (one a different article under the same title; one a periodic template with new figures) | 2 | as the row above |
| Everything else | 229 | counted |

Not detectable by this search: the same story rewritten under another title and another id. Two of the week's articles are the
same story at two outlets inside the week; that is the library's ordinary case, not an exposure.

**Two counts are reported, wider (250 articles) and strict (229).** If they fall on different sides of the rule below, the
result is inconclusive.

## 3. Price and bounds

- **The run, on its own ledger (estimates, not a guarantee):** from the fresh week's charges ($2.5237 for 235 articles: $2.10
  the first step, $0.34 the matching, $0.02 the answer choices, $0.07 the judge) scaled by article count, $2.91; with the first
  step scaled by text length (1.31 million characters against 1.03), $3.15; from July's dearer charge per article (run c1:
  $2.51 the first step and $0.38 the matching for 243 articles), about $3.39. The ledger also holds reservations for calls in
  flight (the judge reserves about $0.013 a call, up to about $0.2 at once). **Ledger ceiling $3.95**, decided explicitly in
  D550 in place of D549's $3.50: a guard below the plausible charge would cut a nearly finished run and waste the whole
  spend. The ledger refuses any attempt beyond it.
- **The readings, bounded in size, their dollar cost unknown:** reader sessions are not calls on the project's provider; the
  wiring design (D448) set them outside the ledger, and the project's price list holds no rate for the two review tools.
  Whether they carry a charge per token on Alex's accounts cannot be seen without reading credentials or settings, which is
  not allowed. No dollar figure is invented, and **the total spending including these sessions is not claimed to be verified
  within $5.** Their bound is in section 4.
- **Against the limits that are enforceable:** paid model calls under D439 before the run about $18.43 of $40; after it at
  most $22.38. D544's $5 checkpoint on paid calls: $0.0022 used; after this run at most $3.95. **Whatever the result, no second
  week fits in what would remain** (the two other later weeks price at about $4.1 and $5.1), so the direction returns to the
  council after this reading in every case.

## 4. What is read, and the reading's capacity

Every written ladder and every refusal of the three attempts **of every topic the week opens** (the topics left out of the
counts are read too, and reported as description), as in July: packets built by the existing builder (at most 22 items a
packet), two reader families apart with the existing form (`clean-arch/step4-2026-11-10/ladder/stage-a-reader-brief.md`), one
session a packet; the marks that differ ruled by a third reader of each family; the collector's report. Claude's own marks on
every attempt are written to a file before the readers' answers are opened.

| Topics opened | Items | First-reader sessions | Third-reader sessions | Bound on input tokens (0.5 million a session) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| up to 7 | up to 21 | 2 | 2 | 2 million |
| 8 to 14 | 24 to 42 | 4 | 2 | 3 million |
| 15 to 22 | 45 to 66 | 6 | up to 4 | 5 million |
| more than 22 | | **not read: the population exceeds the planned reading; returned to the council before any packet is opened** | | |

Comparable single-packet sessions stored in the repository used 0.07 to 0.36 million input tokens (79 to 93% cached) and at
most 3,200 output tokens. A reading is complete only when every item has a valid row from both families and every differing
mark a ruling from both third readers, or is listed as unresolved; no attempt is left unread.

## 5. The rule, fixed before the send (proposed by the council; not Alex's lines)

On the new week's eligible topics alone, `n` of them, three attempts each, in each of the two counts:

- **Too few:** `n` below 6. Nothing is concluded.
- **Clean:** no agreed fault on the four zero-fault lines in any attempt (a question other than the topic's; a part left
  unlisted; an outcome with no range or two; an unjustified refusal); the same favourable end across attempts for every
  company figure; the same due day for at least nine in ten topics; at least `ceil(35n/44)` topics right in two of three
  attempts and at least `ceil(28n/44)` of them right by written choices (at 6 topics: 5 and 4; at 7: 6 and 5; at 8: 7 and 6).
- **Not clean:** anything else, named by its kind below.

The fresh week's seven topics are shown beside the new week with their existing marks and the sensitivity reading of D547;
pooled counts are given as description only and keep that week's two agreed faults.

## 6. What each outcome is evidence of, and what is done next (none passes Stage A; none reverses the direction by itself)

A count of this size describes what was seen; it does not fix a rate or a cause. With the fresh week, a week of 6 to 8 topics
gives 13 to 15 topics from two weeks, which are not independent draws, and July's 11 declined of 40 came from three runs over
the same fourteen days.

| What is seen on the new week | What it is evidence of | What is done next |
|---|---|---|
| Clean, and no topic declined | two weeks outside the tuned days with no refusal and one fault between them. It supports designing an acceptance; it does not settle the step's refusal rate or show that July's problem is gone | the council takes up the design of a reading sized as the first gate's acceptance (its population fixed before any reading; the article database holds only two more later weeks, about 35 topics with these two, short of Alex's 44) |
| A condition or distinction of the topic left out of the choices, agreed by both families | a lead that the fresh week's fault may be a mechanism. Not yet the same mechanism | the source, the request and the model's own account are read for both cases first; a repair design opens only if they show one mechanism on two distinct questions (D545's trigger), and a new version of the frozen step is then its own council decision (D426) |
| A topic declined | a lead only: neither that July's pattern recurs nor that the first step is the cause | each refusal is read against its article and traced (whether the topic was worth a question; which rule the step applied; whether another attempt gave choices); the council reads the result before any stopped line (D473, D477) is discussed |
| Another fault, on one or two attempts (another question asked; an outcome with no range or two; direction or due day not the same) | one case | recorded with its trace and the model's own account; no design from one case |
| Too few topics, the two counts on different sides, more topics than the reading covers, or a zero-fault mark the third readers leave open | nothing about the first gate | said so; the week's library and judgements are kept as material for the later gates; no further week is sent automatically |

## 7. Stops

A failed precondition of the runner (a frozen file changed, a frozen-piece test red); a component that stops after its one
redo; the ledger's refusal; the 300-call limit. Nothing is edited while the run is live. The run is launched detached with a
log and pid file after a network check; its databases are read only after it ends.

## 1. Goal (end to end)

Each question's judgement must receive the facts that can change its answer; facts that no question receives, those that bear on no question, must

## 2. The core blocker (proven)

**The system uses a fact for a question only when the fact "states exactly this question's own figure". An analyst also reasons onward from a fact: the other party's figure in a deal, price and volume for a product's revenue, a product's variants for its launch, and so on. The filing step cannot do this; the judging step reasons onward once it has the facts.**

This one blocker has two faces (described earlier as "two problems"):

- **The parking lot.** Filing does not recognise facts that bear on a question indirectly, so no question takes them; yet to be kept, a fact must
  first be filed (D209, D264). So D273 added the fallback sentence, which parks them in NVIDIA's total-revenue question. Of the reports under the
  total-revenue question, in the part the gold read, 32–39% are ones the standard does not keep, 31–44% are kept but used by none of the 22 questions,
  and only 7–10% are what the gold actually uses to judge total revenue (three draws); 24–44% of the total-revenue question's judgement citations are
  news about other companies or the whole market (Intel graphics-card retail prices, a gas-fired power plant in Taiwan).
- **Narrow questions starve.** Questions that only indirect facts can answer do not receive them: the custom-chip question received none of Broadcom's
  figures in any of the three draws, and judged "below $40 billion" in all three; the operating-margin and NVIDIA capital-spending questions received
  nothing at all and were never judged.

"""Does a first step continued in two parts give what an unbroken run gives? ($0; D551, condition 4.)

the next call in flight. The second part is then run through the real runner and the real transport, with only the network

connection fails the proof. The two parts are merged and compared with the unbroken run, article by article, and as the later
steps read them. Registered expectations; the exit status is non-zero when one fails.

topic missing), SPLIT_MUTANT=skipped-article (the second part skips the cut article), SPLIT_MUTANT=unchecked-second-part (the

import json
import shutil
import sqlite3
import sys
from pathlib import Path

TRACE_COLUMNS = ['sequence', 'input_id', 'before_state', 'request', 'raw_response', 'result', 'after_state', 'status', 'error',

class Refused(Exception):
    """The parts are not the one case this tool continues."""


def read_part(trace_path):
    """A part's run row and trace rows (as dicts, in order)."""
    conn = sqlite3.connect(f'file:{trace_path}?mode=ro', uri=True)
    try:
        manifest, settings, source_items, initial = conn.execute('select manifest, settings, source_items, initial_theses from run').fetchone()
        rows = [dict(zip(TRACE_COLUMNS, row)) for row in conn.execute(f"select {', '.join(TRACE_COLUMNS)} from trace order by sequence")]
    finally:
        conn.close()
    return {'manifest': json.loads(manifest), 'settings': json.loads(settings), 'source_items': json.loads(source_items),
            'initial': json.loads(initial), 'rows': rows}


def first_part(trace_path):
    """The first part, checked: (part, number of complete articles, the cut row or None)."""
    part = read_part(trace_path)
    complete = [row for row in part['rows'] if row['status'] == 'complete']
    others = [row for row in part['rows'] if row['status'] != 'complete']
    ids = part['manifest']['item_ids']
    if not complete:
        raise Refused('the first part completed no article')
    if [row['sequence'] for row in complete] != list(range(1, len(complete) + 1)) or [row['input_id'] for row in complete] != ids[:len(complete)]:
        raise Refused('the complete articles are not the first articles of the manifest in order')
    if len(others) > 1:
        raise Refused(f'{len(others)} rows are not complete: only one call in flight is continued')
    cut = others[0] if others else None
    if cut is not None and (cut['status'] != 'in_flight' or cut['sequence'] != len(complete) + 1 or cut['input_id'] != ids[len(complete)]
                            or cut['raw_response'] is not None or cut['after_state'] is not None):
        raise Refused(f"the row after the complete articles is not a call cut in flight (status {cut['status']})")
    if len(complete) == len(ids):
        raise Refused('the first part is complete: nothing to continue')
    return part, len(complete), cut


def write_inputs(first_folder, second_folder, calls_used, seconds_used):
    """The second part's manifest, starting library, settings and limits. The limits are the first part's less what it used: the
    calls it reserved (the cut one among them) and the seconds its clock ran before the cut."""
    first_folder, second_folder = Path(first_folder), Path(second_folder)
    part, completed, cut = first_part(first_folder / 'trace.sqlite')
    remaining = part['manifest']['item_ids'][completed:]
    state = json.loads(part['rows'][completed - 1]['after_state'])
    limits = json.loads((first_folder / 'limits.json').read_text())
    limits['max_calls'] = limits['max_calls'] - int(calls_used)
    limits['max_seconds'] = limits['max_seconds'] - int(seconds_used)
    if limits['max_calls'] < len(remaining) or limits['max_seconds'] <= 0:
        raise Refused(f"the limits left ({limits['max_calls']} calls, {limits['max_seconds']} seconds) cannot cover {len(remaining)} articles")
    second_folder.mkdir(parents=True)
    (second_folder / 'manifest.json').write_text(json.dumps(dict(part['manifest'], item_ids=remaining, item_limit=len(remaining)), indent=1))
    (second_folder / 'initial.json').write_text(json.dumps(state, ensure_ascii=False, indent=1))
    shutil.copy(first_folder / 'settings.json', second_folder / 'settings.json')
    (second_folder / 'limits.json').write_text(json.dumps(limits, indent=1))
    record = {'continues': str(first_folder / 'trace.sqlite'), 'complete_articles': completed, 'state_after': part['rows'][completed - 1]['input_id'],
              'cut_call': cut['input_id'] if cut else None, 'remaining_articles': len(remaining), 'calls_used': int(calls_used),
              'seconds_used': int(seconds_used), 'reason': 'the machine slept with a call in flight; the call was never answered (D551)'}
    (second_folder / 'continuation.json').write_text(json.dumps(record, indent=1))

def check_second_part(rows, remaining_ids, state):
    """The second part's trace must be a finished run of every remaining article: each article once and in order; each row complete,
    or the one failure the runner itself goes on after (an answer that failed the format check twice); the library carried from
    each article to the next without a break, starting from `state`. Anything else (a part that stopped, a call still in flight,
    rows missing or out of order) is refused: such a part is not merged and nothing later runs on it."""
    if [row['sequence'] for row in rows] != list(range(1, len(rows) + 1)):
        raise Refused("the second part's rows are not numbered in order")
    if [row['input_id'] for row in rows] != list(remaining_ids):
        raise Refused(f"the second part's trace does not hold every remaining article once and in order ({len(rows)} rows for {len(remaining_ids)} articles)")
    library = state
    for row in rows:
        went_on = row['status'] == 'failed' and str(row['error'] or '').startswith('FormatFailure')
        if row['status'] != 'complete' and not went_on:
            raise Refused(f"article {row['sequence']} of the second part is {row['status']}, not complete: {str(row['error'])[:80]}")
        if json.loads(row['before_state']) != library or row['after_state'] is None:
            raise Refused(f"the library is not carried unbroken into article {row['sequence']} of the second part")
        library = json.loads(row['after_state'])

    """A trace that may stand as a draw's completed first step: every article of its manifest once and in order, each complete (or
    the one failure the runner goes on after), the library carried unbroken from the starting library. Returns the number of
    articles; refuses anything else."""
    part = read_part(trace_path)
    check_second_part(part['rows'], part['manifest']['item_ids'], part['initial'])
    return len(part['rows'])


def merge(first_trace, second_trace, output):
    """One trace from the two parts: the first part's complete articles, then the second part's articles renumbered after them.
    Refuses unless the second part starts exactly where the first stopped and is itself finished: the same settings (the limits
    apart, which the second part has less of), the remaining articles in order with the same stored text, the library as it
    stood after the first part's last complete article, and a trace that holds every remaining article (`check_second_part`). The merged run row is the first part's. The column of running reservations goes on from
    the first part's last figure, the cut call's reservation included, since that call was reserved and may have been charged."""
    part, completed, cut = first_part(first_trace)
    second = read_part(second_trace)
    state = json.loads(part['rows'][completed - 1]['after_state'])
    without_limits = lambda settings: {key: value for key, value in settings.items() if key != 'live_limits'}
    if without_limits(second['settings']) != without_limits(part['settings']):
        raise Refused('the two parts ran with different settings')
    if second['manifest']['item_ids'] != part['manifest']['item_ids'][completed:]:
        raise Refused("the second part's articles are not the first part's remaining articles in order")
    if second['source_items'] != part['source_items'][completed:]:
        raise Refused("the second part read different article records than the first part stored for the same articles")
    if second['initial'] != state:
        raise Refused("the second part did not start from the library after the first part's last complete article")
    check_second_part(second['rows'], part['manifest']['item_ids'][completed:], state)
    output = Path(output)
    if output.exists():
        raise Refused(f'{output} exists')
    shutil.copy(first_trace, output)
    conn = sqlite3.connect(output)
    try:
        with conn:
            conn.execute("delete from trace where status != 'complete'")
            conn.execute('attach database ? as second', (f'file:{second_trace}?mode=ro',))
            columns = ', '.join(TRACE_COLUMNS[1:])
            reserved_before = (cut or part['rows'][completed - 1])['reserved_usd'] or 0.0
            selected = columns.replace('reserved_usd', 'reserved_usd + ?')
            conn.execute(f'insert into trace (sequence, {columns}) select sequence + ?, {selected} from second.trace order by sequence',
                         (completed, reserved_before))
            call_columns = ', '.join(row[1] for row in conn.execute('pragma table_info(model_calls)') if row[1] != 'call_id')
            conn.execute(f'insert into model_calls ({call_columns}) select {call_columns} from second.model_calls order by call_id')
        conn.execute('detach database second')
    finally:
        conn.close()
    return {'complete_articles_of_the_first_part': completed, 'articles_of_the_second_part': len(second['rows']), 'merged': str(output)}

# Deck 1: a pilot of Alex's own product-level review (D560), 2026-11-15, $0

**Status: built from stored material; waits for Alex's half hour. It ranks nothing, passes nothing, replaces nothing.**
Council: `../reflection-4/council-codex-2.md` (the minimum design), `council-codex-3.md` (four adjustments, consensus).

## What it is for

Every judgement of quality since 2026-11-10 was made by two families of model readers who do not agree with each other, on
packets Alex never saw. This pilot tries one thing: can Alex himself mark a short deck of the product's actual output, with
known controls mixed in, in about half an hour, and does that give a reading the model readers can then be checked against?

## Material

The stored comparison of the fresh week, 2026-09-22 to 09-28 (235 articles, 232 not sent before; one run of each system from
an empty library): `poc/data/clean-lean-week-2026-11-14/` (old system `week/p1/prod`, new system `week-r2/c1/judge/draw-c1`); the
reading packets and marks in `../week/`; the census of kept facts that reached no answer in `../delivery-class/`. No model is
called. The two model families' marks on the same questions and answers were made on 2026-11-14 and are frozen; they are not
shown on the cards and stay in the sealed key with their scope (question worth: the whole library seen at once; answer
support: the complete request).

## The selection rule (written before the draw; seed 20261115; the draw itself is in the sealed key, outside the repository)

Sixteen distinct cards and three hidden repeats.

1. **New system, six real answers.** Its planted wrong answer is built on question v1, so v1's real answer is left out (a real
   card must not reveal a plant). That leaves exactly six: v2, v3 and v7 (the three questions of D508's confirmed pairs, which
   carry the completeness sheets) and v4, v5, v6.
2. **Old system, six real answers of fifteen.** First the planted wrong answer is drawn (rule 4) and its question left out.
   Then one independently confirmed supported control is drawn at random from those the separate reader confirmed
   (`../week/controls-B.json`, `control-confirmation.jsonl`); then five more at random from the remaining questions.
3. **Two matters with no question:** M01 (fiscal 2027 revenue: both families mark it missed by one system) and M04 (supply
   commitments: missed by the other), from `../week/matters-A2.json`. The card shows the matter and its source articles; answer
   support is not applicable.
4. **Two wrong answers, one per system:** the new system's planted answer (item 1 of the week's reading B: the rung moved),
   and one of the old system's two planted answers whose cited statements are all stored (items 22 and 24; the third plant
   cites an added statement), drawn at random. Each keeps the request and the answer choices of its original control. Both
   model families marked all four plants unsupported on 2026-11-14.
5. **Three hidden repeats:** drawn at random from the real answers among the first ten cards in the order that carry no
   completeness sheet (so a repeat is the same card as its original). *Changed before any card was seen: the first build
   failed on a repeat of a sheet card.*
6. **Order:** the sixteen shuffled; the last six positions and the three repeats shuffled together.
7. **Completeness sheets on three cards** (new system v2, v3, v7): the confirmed kept-but-undelivered fact of that question
   (D508; for v2 one fact reported by three articles) and one negative control drawn at random from the kept statements both
   first census readers, reading every statement against all seven questions, left empty for this question while naming it
   for another (a substantive fact), not linked to it and not among its candidates. *Changed before any card was seen: no
   candidate of v3 or v7 was marked not bearing by both fresh readers, so the control comes from the first readers' pass.*
   On every other card completeness is not assessed.

## A card

The question; whose it is and its due day; its answer choices with the present answer marked; the answer's stated reasons;
the statements it cites, each with its passage and a link to the stored article; and, one click away, the complete request
the answer step was shown. No system name. Blinding is imperfect in two known ways: the two systems' requests are worded a
little differently, and the two wrong answers were built on earlier days' requests (2026-09-22) while most real answers are of
the week's last day; each card shows the true day of the answer it carries.

## Alex's marks

Per card: **worth tracking** (yes / no / cannot tell); **answer supported by what is shown** (yes / no / cannot tell); a few
words. Per fact on a completeness sheet: **bears on this question** (yes / no / cannot tell), then **it would change**: the
answer / only the confidence / neither / cannot tell. Opening the complete request or an article is allowed and recorded by
the page, with the time spent.

## What is reported afterwards

Every mark. His marks on the three repeats beside their originals. His marks beside each model family's stored marks on the
same cards. Whether the two wrong answers were rejected and the confirmed supported controls accepted. His answers on the
completeness sheets beside the census readers'. The time, and where it went. The classes of what he rejects, in his words.

**Signals for redesign, not a pass line:** two repeats marked differently; both wrong answers accepted; the deck not markable
in about half an hour. Three repeats and two wrong answers are too few for an error rate; perfect marks would not prove the
method reliable.

**It cannot show:** a usable share for any system; which system is better; what the cards' selection left out; a rate for
other news; which step caused a bad card. $0 covers model calls only: Alex's time and the preparation are not priced.

## To open it

`deck-1.html` in this folder, in a browser. Marks are kept in the browser as he goes; the last box on the page holds them as
text to paste back.

**I would not send the proposed two-week run yet.** The next step should be a **$0 proof of the continuation and downstream replay**, followed by the existing Deck 1 review. That gives Alex the review already prepared and establishes whether a later paid run would actually represent a library carried through time.

For example, the current continuation code explicitly refuses a first segment that is already complete. It was built to resume an interrupted run, so its existing proof does not establish that it can append a new week to a completed one. [Continuation code](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/second-week/continuation.py), [split proof](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/second-week/split_proof.py)

**(a) The next step.** I support testing a carried library end to end, but the proposal is not yet a decision-ready test of the product condition.

- The six model accounts support the reported leads, but they are **later explanations**, not proof of the causes. In particular, the model calls both links word-overlap errors after being asked; the two reader families also disagreed with earlier D508 readers about whether the growth outlook bears on supply commitments. Read that as a disputed relevance case, not a proven general mechanism. [Model accounts](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/carried-library/model-accounts.json), [D508 census](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/delivery-class/CLASS-CENSUS-RESULT.md)
- D560’s pilot is **already built** and uses stored actual answers. Replace it with a future deck only after Alex’s decision: the existing deck tests whether his reading works on material with prior model-reader marks and controls. A new deck would have different material and would need those controls rebuilt. [Deck 1 design](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/pilot-deck-1/DESIGN.md)
- Alex’s request to execute is a reason to proceed with the authorized $0 work. It does not by itself establish that D559’s wider starting-library question has been answered, or that he has approved this particular paid run. D561 explicitly separates those questions. [D561](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/DECISIONS-log.md:7105)

**(b) Two weeks, if the proofs hold; no third week yet.** Two weeks can provide one bounded example of continuation. A third week would increase cost without fixing the uncertainty about reader reliability or showing how much two draws of the same setup differ. One resulting library cannot establish a rate or a winner.

**(c) The readings and stopping rule need revision before a send.**

- The **90% supported** line is a proposed threshold, not Alex’s accepted line. In the fresh-week reading, one family rejected **two of four** independently confirmed supported controls. Without a reliable reading, crossing or missing 90% can reflect the reader rather than the system. [Fresh-week result](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/week/WEEK-RESULT.md)
- “Every last answer follows from what it was shown” cannot detect important facts omitted from the request. Add a separately bounded source-to-answer check with a known positive **group** and a negative control. Report missing questions, unanswered questions, refused answer choices, unsupported answers and unresolved reader disagreements separately; an unanswered question must not disappear from the denominator. The earlier delivery reading had no proven positive control for a single missing fact. [Trial result](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/TRIAL-RESULT.md), [comparison sizing](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/comparison/COMPARISON-SIZING.md)
- “Two re-openings” needs a defined population, an independent same-question reading and controls for lost worthwhile questions and evidence. Two duplicate openings among two opportunities and among fifty opportunities mean different things. Keep a “cannot tell” outcome.
- This would be a **new two-week replay of later steps**, not automatically the live product’s existing two-week history. It must say whether it preserves or regenerates the first week’s matching, answer choices, judgements and their state; both routes answer different questions.

**(d) Required $0 proofs before any send:**

1. **Inputs and chronology.** Prove the starting trace is complete, its last library is exactly the second week’s first input, and all IDs, source text, ordering and dates match the intended manifests. I verified that the proposed manifest has **241 unique IDs** and exactly the same ID set as the frozen fresh list for those dates. Its order differs from that list, although its days are ordered; prove the within-day order against the actual source/run order rather than assuming the lists are interchangeable. [Manifest](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/carried-run/manifest-2026-09-29-10-05.json), [fresh list](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/fresh-articles-2026-09-22-10-05.json)
2. **Continuation and identity.** On stored data, prove an appended completed segment preserves every article, question ID, state transition and failed item, and that the combined trace is accepted by the actual downstream entry points. Mutants must catch a dropped article, wrong starting library, duplicate ID and broken state transition. The existing merge handles a different case and does not prove this.
3. **Downstream and time.** Replay stored answers through matching, grouping, answer choices and judging; compare requests, links, opening dates and outputs at each boundary. Prove no future question or evidence reaches an earlier judgement. The adapter processes days and has a due-date guard, but the proposed new concatenation has not itself been proved. [Judging adapter](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/clean-arch/step4-2026-11-10/stage_b/ladder_adapter.py:263)
4. **Reader and spend controls.** Reconstruct the exact requests and source packets; demonstrate the supported and wrong controls are not identifiable by duplication or dates; exercise the missing-fact control; account for all attempted calls, retries and stops under one ledger. Price the actual complete request population and reader workload. The proposed $6 ceiling is a reservation, not evidence that all stages will finish inside it.

The result would still be one company, one continued period and one draw. It could reveal concrete failures and produce material for Alex to inspect; it could not establish general production readiness.

**CONSENSUS: no, because** the proposed send and its 90% stopping line are not yet supported by a proved continuation, a reliable reader check, or a decision to replace the prepared pilot.
